text:
All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police services in Nigeria, paving the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.
The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday, November 16, 2026.
According to the statement, the unanimous approval represents 100 per cent endorsement by the state legislatures, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.
The bill, titled, “A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for Related Matters,” seeks to provide the constitutional framework for establishing state police across the country.
Ogunlana explained that the bill had earlier fulfilled all constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission, but the leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all the states.
He described the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the National Assembly and state legislatures.
According to him, the development also reflects constructive collaboration between the executive arms of government at the federal and state levels.
“Following the completion of the verification process by my Office, the Bill is set for transmission to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for His Excellency’s assent,” the statement read.
The Clerk described the development as a major milestone in the ongoing efforts to reform Nigeria’s policing system.
He added that the achievement would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to complete and transmit other Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the State Houses of Assembly for consideration.
The leadership of the National Assembly also commended the 36 state governors, Speakers and members of the State Houses of Assembly, as well as other stakeholders, for their cooperation and commitment to reforming the country’s policing system.
